relations: Aaron and Kayla — abusive ex-partner who imprisoned her and has now tracked her down: “You were supposed to come back to me when I got out.”; “You held me on a fucking leash.”

Vero and Kayla — she has never told him she thinks she loves him: “I haven’t told Vero that I think I love him back”; she trusts her instinct that something was wrong was because “Clay trusted my feeling that something wasn’t right”
Clay and Kayla — protective of her and possessive of her: “Clay trusted my feeling that something wasn’t right, and I hold on to that thought.”; “or told Clay I actually like him calling me his”

Brawley and Vero — Brawley is the man who loves Vero: “Nor have I confided in Brawley how he makes me feel just because he loves Vero so much, and how I want him to love me with even a sliver of that intensity.”
Ares and Kayla — one of the four men she would call on: “There are four men who would kill for me, but I can’t get their attention.”; “And I want to tell Ares that I need him.”

facts.fact: On the walk back Kayla's hands blur and her body stops cooperating — the drug is taking effect
facts.anchor: I don’t make it more than a few steps when my hands begin feeling weird, and when I look down at them, they blur.

facts.fact: Aaron steps out of the cornstalk and greets her as “care bear”
Aaron admits he drugged her and that she was never going to get away from him
facts.anchor: But the drug speeds up the inevitable. You were never getting away from me, care bear. You know that.

facts.fact: Aaron drags her behind the cornfield toward the cemetery and shows her an open grave site fitted with a coffin
facts.anchor: He stops walking and stares down at the open grave site, fitted with a coffin.

facts.fact: Aaron states his possessive logic — if he cannot have Kayla, no one gets to have her
facts.anchor: If I can’t have you, then no one gets to. That’s how this works. Forever, that is what you told me once, and I gave you everything.

facts.fact: Aaron drops Kayla into the coffin and then pushes the lid closed over her
facts.anchor: Aaron shakes his head and pulls himself out of the hole, then leans down and pushes the lid closed.

facts.fact: Buried and fading, Kayla confesses to herself the feelings she never told the four men — love for Vero, that she likes Clay calling her his, what Brawley means to her, and that she needs Ares
facts.anchor: I haven’t told Vero that I think I love him back, or told Clay I actually like him calling me his.

facts.fact: Aaron recites the Scarecrow riddle over the closed coffin and says this makes two Scarecrows
facts.anchor: For I am the Scarecrow, and that now makes two.
